title: Beyond Math, Code, and Logic: Do Reasoning Models Transfer to Scientific Argumentation?
abstract: arXiv:2611.27722v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Scientific discourse depends on argumentative reasoning: identifying claims, evaluating evidence, and constructing coherent responses. While recent advances in reasoning-capable language models have demonstrated strong performance on mathematical, coding, and logical benchmarks, their ability to engage in scientific argumentation remains unclear. We present the first systematic evaluation of language models across seven tasks spanning argument mining, rebuttal generation, and discourse-level reasoning using research papers, peer reviews, and grant proposals. Our study reveals that even frontier models with strong general reasoning skills struggle with domain-specific argumentative tasks, highlighting a fundamental capability gap. To address this, we introduce a training framework that explicitly scaffolds the argumentative reasoning process in language models, substantially improving their competence in scientific discourse. translated_title: 超越数学、代码与逻辑：推理模型能否迁移至科学论证？
translated_abstract: 科学论述依赖于论证性推理：识别论点、评估证据以及构建连贯的回应。尽管近年来具备推理能力的语言模型在数学、编程和逻辑基准测试中表现出色，但它们参与科学论证的能力仍不明确。我们首次对语言模型进行了系统性评估，涵盖七项任务，包括论证挖掘、反驳生成和话语层面的推理，使用的数据来自研究论文、同行评审和科研基金申请书。我们的研究表明，即使是拥有强大通用推理能力的前沿模型，在处理领域特定的论证任务时也会遇到困难，这凸显了一个根本性的能力差距。为解决这一问题，我们引入了一个训练框架，显式地为语言模型的论证推理过程搭建脚手架，从而显著提升了它们在科学论述中的能力。
tldr: 该研究首次系统评估了语言模型在科学论证任务上的表现，发现即使前沿推理模型在领域特定论证任务上仍存在根本性能力差距，并提出了一种显式搭建论证推理脚手架的训练框架，显著提升了模型的科学论述能力。
